title: Mode-Level Authenticated Encryption Against Message Comparison Attacks
summary: No mode-level authenticated-encryption solution is currently known to limit Message Comparison success to a negligible value; construct one that achieves this.

formal_statement.body: Construct a mode-level authenticated-encryption solution secure against Message Comparison attacks in the following leakage setting: sample $K \leftarrow \{0,1\}^n$ and $b \leftarrow \{0,1\}$, and give an adversary $X_0$, $X_1$, and challenge leakage $L(X_b,K)$. Its goal is to recover $b$, equivalently to determine whether the leakage was produced using $X_0$ or $X_1$. No mode-level solution is currently known that limits this success probability to a negligible value; the required construction must achieve such a bound.

scope.domain: Mode-level authenticated encryption under physical-leakage Message Comparison attacks.
parameters: K: an n-bit key sampled from {0,1}^n
b: a binary challenge bit sampled from {0,1}
scope.unresolved_remainder: Construct a mode-level authenticated-encryption solution that limits the Message Comparison success probability to a negligible value.

citations.label: Mode-Level vs. Implementation-Level Physical Security in Symmetric Cryptography: A Practical Guide Through the Leakage-Resistance Jungle

progress.summary: The source presents Message Comparison as distinguishing whether challenge leakage came from X0 or X1, and reports that no mode-level solution is known to make the success probability negligible. It frames the remaining work as constructing such a solution.
citation_labels: Davide Bellizia et al., Mode-Level vs. Implementation-Level Physical Security in Symmetric Cryptography: A Practical Guide Through the Leakage-Resistance Jungle
